title: Yield Relationships & Bond Math

sections.heading: The 4 Yields — Definitions
items: Nominal Yield (Coupon/Stated): FIXED % of par set at issue. Never changes. 6% coupon = $60/yr forever.
Current Yield (CY): Annual coupon ÷ Current Market Price. Ignores gain/loss at maturity.
Yield to Maturity (YTM): Annualized total return if held to maturity. Includes coupon + amortization of discount/premium. Also called 'basis'.
Yield to Call (YTC): Same as YTM but uses call date & call price. Accelerates discount gain OR premium loss.

sections.heading: Core Formulas
items: CY = Annual Coupon ÷ Market Price
Tax-Equivalent Yield (TEY) = Muni Yield ÷ (1 − Tax Bracket)
Muni-Equivalent of Corp = Corp Yield × (1 − Tax Bracket)
Bond Price ($) = Quoted Price × 10  (e.g., 'trading at 97' = $970)
1 point = $10 = 1% of par  |  1 basis point (bp) = 0.01% = 1/100 of 1%  |  100 bps = 1%

items.Memory Aid: Going UP to par = gain accelerates if called

items.Order (high\u2192low): Nominal > CY > YTC > YTM (some sources YTM > YTC)
items.Memory Aid: Coming DOWN to par = loss accelerates if called → YTC is LOWEST for premium

sections.heading: Premium Bond — Critical Exam Point
items: For a PREMIUM callable bond: YTC is the LOWEST yield (worst case for investor).
For a DISCOUNT callable bond: YTC is the HIGHEST yield.
Rule: Quote the YIELD TO WORST — premium = YTC; discount = YTM.

sections.heading: Quick Numerical Examples
items: Investor in 30% bracket; muni yields 7% → TEY = 7%/(1−.30) = 10%.
Corp yields 11%, 30% bracket → after-tax = 11% × .70 = 7.7%.
'Bond trading on 5.83 basis' = YTM is 5.83%.

sections.heading: Points vs Basis Points (do NOT confuse)
Accrued Interest Mechanics
items: Buyer PAYS seller accrued interest at settlement (added to price).
Buyer is reimbursed by receiving the FULL next coupon from issuer.
Interest accrues from last coupon date UP TO BUT NOT INCLUDING settlement date.
Bonds in default trade 'flat' (no accrued interest); income bonds also trade flat.

sections.heading: Inverse Price/Yield Relationship
items: Interest rates ↑ → Bond prices ↓ → CY, YTM, YTC all ↑
Interest rates ↓ → Bond prices ↑ → CY, YTM, YTC all ↓
Coupon (nominal) NEVER changes regardless of price movement.
Longer maturity + lower coupon = MORE volatile (higher duration).

common_traps: Confusing POINTS ($10 = price) with BASIS POINTS (0.01% = yield). A bond 'up 30 basis points' is a YIELD move, not price.
Forgetting that on a PREMIUM bond, YTC is the LOWEST yield (issuer calls when rates fall = worst case). On a DISCOUNT bond, YTC is the HIGHEST.
Using the wrong tax formula: TEY = muni ÷ (1 − bracket). Don't multiply when going FROM muni TO corporate equivalent.
Saying coupon changes when price changes — it does NOT. Only CY/YTM/YTC move with price.
Charging accrued interest on zero-coupon bonds or bonds in default — neither pays accrued interest (trade flat).
Mixing day-count: Treasuries use actual/actual; corporates & munis use 30/360.
